doc.cra-noa.name: notice of assessment
doc.cra-noa.title: Notice of assessment
doc.cra-noa.hint: After the CRA processes your tax return
doc.cra-noa.what: Your notice of assessment (NOA) is the CRA’s summary of your tax return after processing: the amounts it calculated, and whether you get a refund, owe money or neither.
doc.cra-noa.step.compare.title: Compare it with your return
doc.cra-noa.step.compare.detail: Check the line amounts. If the CRA changed anything, the notice explains why.
doc.cra-noa.step.refund.title: Watch for your refund
doc.cra-noa.step.refund.detail: Track it in your CRA account. The CRA may keep some or all of it if you owe a tax balance or another government debt, like a student loan.
doc.cra-noa.step.pay.title: Pay what you owe
doc.cra-noa.step.pay.detail: Pay online, by mail or in person. Can’t pay it all at once? You can arrange to pay over time.
doc.cra-noa.step.change.title: Fix a mistake
doc.cra-noa.step.change.detail: Forgot something or made an error? Use Change my return in your CRA account, or ReFILE in your tax software.
doc.cra-noa.step.object.title: Disagree? You can object
doc.cra-noa.step.object.detail: If your return was complete but you disagree with the assessment, file an objection online in your CRA account or with Form T400A.
doc.cra-noa.step.keep.title: Keep it for next year
doc.cra-noa.step.keep.detail: It shows your RRSP deduction limit and the access code tax software asks for.
doc.cra-noa.look.1.title: Notice details
doc.cra-noa.look.1.detail: The tax year, the date issued and the last 4 digits of your SIN.
doc.cra-noa.look.2.title: Account summary
doc.cra-noa.look.2.detail: Your result at a glance: “Refund”, “Amount due” or “Balance: Nil”.
doc.cra-noa.look.3.title: Tax assessment
doc.cra-noa.look.3.detail: The key line amounts used to calculate your result. Compare them with your return.
doc.cra-noa.look.4.title: Explanation of changes
doc.cra-noa.look.4.detail: Why the CRA changed anything on your return.
doc.cra-noa.look.5.title: RRSP and FHSA room
doc.cra-noa.look.5.detail: Your RRSP deduction limit and FHSA participation room for next year, if they apply.
doc.cra-noa.look.6.title: Access code
doc.cra-noa.look.6.detail: 8 letters and numbers on the right side. Tax software asks for it when you file.
doc.cra-nor.name: notice of reassessment
doc.cra-nor.title: Notice of reassessment
doc.cra-nor.hint: When an assessed return is changed
doc.cra-nor.what: A notice of reassessment (NOR) is an updated summary the CRA sends only when your already-assessed return changes: because you asked, or after a review.
doc.cra-nor.step.why.title: Read the explanation of changes
doc.cra-nor.step.why.detail: It says what changed on your return and why.
doc.cra-nor.step.refund.title: Watch for your refund
doc.cra-nor.step.refund.detail: Track it in your CRA account. The CRA may keep some or all of it if you owe a tax balance or another government debt, like a student loan.
doc.cra-nor.step.pay.title: Pay what you owe
doc.cra-nor.step.pay.detail: Pay online, by mail or in person. Can’t pay it all at once? You can arrange to pay over time.
doc.cra-nor.step.newInfo.title: Have more receipts or documents?
doc.cra-nor.step.newInfo.detail: If a claim changed after a review, the CRA accepts new documents and looks at the claim again.
doc.cra-nor.step.object.title: Disagree? You can object
doc.cra-nor.step.object.detail: If you disagree with the reassessment, file an objection online in your CRA account or with Form T400A.
doc.cra-nor.look.1.title: Notice details
doc.cra-nor.look.1.detail: The tax year and the date this reassessment was issued.
doc.cra-nor.look.2.title: Account summary
doc.cra-nor.look.2.detail: Your new result: a refund, an amount due or a nil balance.
doc.cra-nor.look.3.title: Explanation of changes
doc.cra-nor.look.3.detail: What the CRA changed on your return, and why.
doc.cra-review.name: CRA review letter
doc.cra-review.title: Review letter
doc.cra-review.hint: The CRA asks for receipts or documents
doc.cra-review.what: A review letter means the CRA wants to confirm something you claimed, like a credit or a deduction. Being selected for a review is not an audit.
doc.cra-review.step.deadline.title: Reply by the date in the letter
doc.cra-review.step.deadline.detail: Send everything within the time frame it gives, to the address in the letter.
doc.cra-review.step.reference.title: Include the reference number
doc.cra-review.step.reference.detail: It’s in the upper right corner of the letter.
doc.cra-review.step.upload.title: Upload your documents
doc.cra-review.step.upload.detail: Use Submit documents in your CRA account instead of mailing copies.
doc.cra-review.step.missing.title: Missing a receipt?
doc.cra-review.step.missing.detail: Send a written explanation, or call the number at the bottom of the letter.
doc.cra-review.step.time.title: Need more time?
doc.cra-review.step.time.detail: Call the number at the bottom of the letter before the deadline.
doc.cra-review.look.1.title: Reference number
doc.cra-review.look.1.detail: Upper right corner. Include it with everything you send.
doc.cra-review.look.2.title: What the CRA needs
doc.cra-review.look.2.detail: The receipts or documents requested, and the date to reply by.
doc.cra-review.look.3.title: Phone number
doc.cra-review.look.3.detail: At the bottom of the letter: for questions, or to ask for more time.
doc.cra-ccb-notice.name: Canada child benefit notice
doc.cra-ccb-notice.title: Canada child benefit notice
doc.cra-ccb-notice.hint: Your child benefit from July to June
doc.cra-ccb-notice.what: Your Canada child benefit (CCB) notice shows how much you’ll get and the information the CRA used to calculate it. Amounts are recalculated every July from last year’s tax return.
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.check.title: Check the details it used
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.check.detail: Marital status, children in your care, address: if anything is wrong or out of date, tell the CRA so it can recalculate.
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.file.title: File your taxes every year
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.file.detail: You and your spouse or partner both need to file by April 30, even with no income, or payments can stop.
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.overpaid.title: Paid too much?
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.overpaid.detail: An overpayment notice comes with a remittance voucher. The CRA may keep future payments until it’s repaid.
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.update.title: Update your information online
doc.cra-ccb-notice.step.update.detail: Most changes can be made in your CRA account.
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.name: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit notice
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.title: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit notice
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.what: The Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB) replaced the GST/HST credit in July 2026. Your notice shows your tax-free quarterly payments, based on last year’s tax return.
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.quarterly.title: Four payments a year
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.quarterly.detai: Payments come in July, October, January and April, and are recalculated every July.
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.small.title: Small amounts come at once
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.small.detail: If it works out to less than $50 a quarter, you get the whole amount in July.
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.missing.title: Payment didn’t arrive?
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.missing.detail: Wait 10 business days after the payment date, and check your CRA account before you call.
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.update.title: Keep your information up to date
doc.cra-cgeb-notice.step.update.detail: Most changes can be made in your CRA account.
doc.esdc-ei-decision.name: EI decision letter
doc.esdc-ei-decision.title: EI decision letter
doc.esdc-ei-decision.hint: Service Canada’s decision on your EI claim
doc.esdc-ei-decision.what: An EI decision letter tells you what Service Canada decided about your Employment Insurance claim, for example that benefits were denied or that you have to repay some.
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.read.title: Read the reason for the decision
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.read.detail: The letter explains what the decision is based on.
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.newInfo.title: Send new information first
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.newInfo.detail: Documents or details you haven’t given yet may change the decision without a reconsideration.
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.reconsider.det: Fill out, print and sign Form INS5210, then submit it in person or by mail. It’s free.
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.late.title: Past 30 days?
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.late.detail: You can still ask, but you’ll need to explain why it’s late.
doc.esdc-ei-decision.step.call.title: Questions about your claim
doc.esdc-ei-statement.name: EI benefit statement
doc.esdc-ei-statement.title: EI benefit statement
doc.esdc-ei-statement.what: Your EI benefit statement confirms your claim and gives you a 4-digit access code. You need the code and your SIN every time you submit an EI report.
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.code.title: Keep your access code safe
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.code.detail: Store it separately from your SIN. Entering it counts as signing your report.
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.every2.title: Report every 2 weeks
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.every2.detail: Your reports show you’re still eligible and keep your payments coming.
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.how.title: Report online or by phone
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.how.detail: Use the Internet Reporting System, or call {phone}.
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.calendar.titl: Track your hours as you go
doc.esdc-ei-statement.step.calendar.deta: The reporting calendar makes each report quicker.
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.name: Old Age Security enrolment letter
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.title: OAS enrolment letter
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.what: If you got this letter around your 64th birthday, you’re enrolled in Old Age Security automatically. You don’t need to apply.
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.nothing.titl: Most people don’t need to do anything
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.nothing.deta: Your pension starts on its own.
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.check.title: Check the information in the letter
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.check.detail: If something is wrong, or the letter asks you to apply, you need to act.
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.delay.title: Want to start later?
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.delay.detail: You can delay your pension or change your start date online in My Service Canada Account.
doc.esdc-oas-enrolment.step.call.title: Questions?
doc.ircc-biometrics.name: biometric instruction letter
doc.ircc-biometrics.title: Biometric instruction letter
doc.ircc-biometrics.hint: IRCC asks for fingerprints and a photo
doc.ircc-biometrics.what: A biometric instruction letter (BIL) confirms you need to give your fingerprints and photo, and tells you how to book an appointment.
doc.ircc-biometrics.step.book.title: Book your appointment now
doc.ircc-biometrics.step.book.detail: You have 30 days from when you got the letter. Book as soon as you can to avoid delays.
doc.ircc-biometrics.step.bring.title: Bring the letter and your passport
doc.ircc-biometrics.step.bring.detail: You need your BIL and a valid passport at the appointment.
doc.ircc-biometrics.step.more.title: Can’t make it within 30 days?
doc.ircc-biometrics.step.more.detail: Use the IRCC web form to explain why, and include your appointment date.
doc.ircc-biometrics.look.1.title: Important information
doc.ircc-biometrics.look.1.detail: The section with details specific to your application.
doc.ircc-biometrics.look.2.title: How to book
doc.ircc-biometrics.look.2.detail: Where and how to book your biometrics appointment.
doc.ircc-medical.name: medical instructions letter
doc.ircc-medical.title: Medical exam instructions
doc.ircc-medical.what: Your medical exam instructions tell you to see an IRCC-approved panel physician for your permanent residence medical exam.
doc.ircc-medical.step.panel.title: Choose a panel physician
doc.ircc-medical.step.panel.detail: Only a doctor on IRCC’s panel list can do the exam. Your own doctor can’t.
doc.ircc-medical.step.within.title: Go within 30 days
doc.ircc-medical.step.within.detail: Get the exam within 30 days of getting these instructions.
doc.ircc-medical.step.follow.title: Follow the instructions exactly
doc.ircc-medical.step.follow.detail: If you don’t, IRCC may refuse your application.
doc.ircc-medical.step.status.title: Track your application
sig.gift-cards: Asks you to pay with gift cards or prepaid credit cards
sig.crypto: Asks for payment in cryptocurrency, like Bitcoin
sig.etransfer: Sends a refund or demands payment by Interac e-Transfer
sig.threats: Threatens arrest, deportation or prison, or uses aggressive language
sig.text-message: Came as a text, WhatsApp or Messenger message (other than a sign-in code you just asked for)
sig.link-info: Has a link asking for personal or banking information
sig.fake-website: Uses a web address that isn’t canada.ca or cra-arc.gc.ca
sig.public-meeting: Wants to meet in a public place to collect a payment

scam.real.title: How to check it’s real
scam.real.1: Sign in to your CRA account. Real notices and mail are there.
scam.real.2: Call the CRA yourself at {phone}. Never use a number from the message.
scam.real.3: Real CRA web addresses start with canada.ca or end in cra-arc.gc.ca.
scam.do.title: If you think it’s a scam
scam.do.1: Don’t pay, click links or share any information.
scam.do.2: Report it to the CRA at {phone} so it can protect your account.
scam.do.3: Tell the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at {phone}, even if you didn’t lose anything.

identify.scam.ask: Is this CRA letter real or a scam?

identify.forms.hint: Find the official page for any common form
identify.tip: Before you share a photo, cover your SIN and any account numbers. They’re never needed here.

forms.pdf.body: Download the form to your computer first. Fillable government PDFs often don’t work in a web browser or on a phone.

forms.empty.body: This finder covers the most-used CRA, Service Canada and IRCC forms. Another federal department may publish the one you need: find it in the official list, or try the form number.
forms.passport.title: Passport forms depend on your situation
forms.passport.body: Adults, children, renewals and replacements each use a different form. Answer the questions on the passport pages to get the right one.
forms.error.title: We couldn’t search forms just now
